speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing mental status changes; to help me understand your condition, could you please describe exactly what symptoms you are feeling and when they started?

REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, CBC, TSH, Urine_Tox_Screen.

REQUEST IMAGES: Non-contrast_head_CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Na: 122 mEq/L, K: 3.9 mEq/L, HCO3: 24 mEq/L, BUN: 21 mg/dL, Cr: 0.9 mg/dL, Ca: 8.5 mg/dL, Glu: 105 mg/dL, Urine Osmolality: 334 mOsm/kg, Urine Na: 45 mEq/L, Urine Glu: 0 mg/dL

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old female. The patient has been brought to the emergency room by her family due to altered mental status. The family mentions that she has been increasingly confused over the past few days. No recent head trauma or known drug use. The patient has a smoking history of 30 pack-years.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mental status changes. I also have Increased confusion, Lethargy. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I have ordered the necessary blood work, a tox screen, and a head CT to investigate your confusion and lethargy. While you wait for those results, can you tell me if you have recently experienced any head trauma, seizures, or if you have been taking any new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Patient has a history of hypertension, managed with medication. No other significant medical history is reported. Social history: Patient is a smoker with a 30 pack-year history. Drinks alcohol socially. No illicit drug use is reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of hypertension, smoking, and current presentation with confusion and lethargy, I need to know if you have any specific symptoms like vision changes, severe headaches, or weakness on one side of your body.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypertensive Encephalopathy
